svg.title: HyperWeave
svg.desc: HyperWeave Noctilucent Monolith footer (adaptive). One quantised ice field shows through the octahedron's chamber and the wordmark. Its bands refract and flow like liquid on incommensurate phi-period currents, so the pattern never repeats.

hw:reasoning.hw:intent: Let the ice inside the letters move like a slow current: subtle, continuous, and never the same twice.
hw:reasoning.hw:approach: The motion lives inside the filters, as SMIL, so it runs wherever the SVG renders. Each terrain is displaced by a second, low-frequency noise field. That warp field meanders on its own current, which makes the ice bands refract and flow like liquid, and the displacement strength swells and relaxes. The terrain itself drifts on a slower, separate current. The dithered stratum runs a different current from the base, so its bands slide through the base bands. Glints ride a third current. All periods are phi powers, some times pi, so the joint state never recurs.
hw:reasoning.hw:tradeoffs: The filters re-run every frame (two noise fields per stratum), which costs far more than a composite. SMIL ignores prefers-reduced-motion; only the singularity pulse honours it. The adaptive file defaults to dark; where the host makes prefers-color-scheme inert, ship dark and light through a picture element.
hw:reasoning.hw:constraints-applied: zero-js, zero-background, zero-borders, reduced-motion, smil-filter-currents, quasi-periodic
